chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abd al-Rahman, from whom he narrated, who said:

"Do not inherit from the grandfathers except three: the father of the mother, the father of the father, and the father of the father of the father." Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: "These two reports are not acted upon because they are mursal (disconnected) and not musnad (connected), and because the higher grandfather does not inherit alongside the nearer grandfather; rather, the nearer grandfather acquires the wealth to the exclusion of the higher one. And that which indicates this is what he narrated:"

key_terms.أَبُ أَبِي الْأَبِ: father of the father of the father (paternal grandfather of the paternal grandfather)
key_terms.الْأَجْدَادِ: grandfathers (plural of grandparent on father's or mother's side)
key_terms.مُرْسَلَانِ: disconnected reports (where a successor narrates directly from the Prophet or Imam without mentioning the companion)
key_terms.مُسْنَدَيْنِ: connected reports (with a complete chain of narrators)

ai.seo_question: Which grandfathers are entitled to inherit according to Shia hadith, and does the nearer grandfather exclude the distant one?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the specific hierarchy of grandfathers in Shia inheritance law, limiting inheritors to the maternal grandfather, paternal grandfather, and paternal grandfather of the father. Shaykh al-Tusi highlights that while these reports exist, they are often considered *mursal* (disconnected) and thus not the primary basis for legal rulings. The text clarifies the principle of *hajb* (exclusion), where the nearest male ancestor in the paternal line excludes more distant ones, a rule supported by further evidences in the chapter.
